newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher as electronics rebound.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher as electronics rebound.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher on Saturday as the electronics sector rebounded strongly after recent heavy profit-taking, brokers said.
The weighted index finished 59.33 points or 0.73 percent higher at 8,141.12, adding to Friday's 1.07 percent gain.
Turnover in Saturday's two-hour session was T$62.3 billion, down from Friday's T$98.5 billion in three hours' trade.
Electronics rebounded, rising 2.4 percent. Chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor closed up T$4.50 to T$102, while another chipmaker, United Microelectronics, put on T$2.50 to T$66.50.

"Electronics rebounded after recent heavy profit-taking, but as electronics will face its relatively weak sales season in the second quarter, I don't expect any sharp gains for the sector," said Michael Hung, an independent analyst.
Electrical, cement and construction sector shares were also strong, but financials, the major recent gainers, fell slightly.
Brokers also attributed the rise partly to reflect a higher than expected first-quarter gross domestic product growth.
A state statistics agency said on Friday that Taiwan's first-quarter GDP grew 6.83 percent year-on-year, well above its February forecast of 6.40 percent.
Hung said the slowing turnover and stable prices indicated the index seemed to have reached initial support at around 8,000-8,100 after its recent corrections.
Shares were pummelled earlier this week by political worries.
Jitters over unsettled domestic politics are easing after President Lee Teng-hui promised at a news conference on Thursday that Premier Lien Chan will step down in July, brokers said.
Brokers saw a firming trend next week within a narrow 8,100-8,250 range.
